ask: Why is it on the path?
cards: The faith began among the followers of Jesus of Nazareth, a Jewish teacher crucified around 30 CE, and became the religion of the Roman Empire in the 4th century.
Matthew and Luke agree that Jesus was born in Bethlehem in the reign of Herod but state no date; only Matthew has the wise men, only Luke the shepherds.
The magi were priests of Zoroastrianism and earlier Iranian religions; in Matthew, magi from the east pay homage to the infant Jesus, rendered in English as kings or wise men.
The earliest document to place the birth on 25 December was written in Rome in 336; the day was the traditional date of the winter solstice in the Roman Empire.
The 4th-century bishop of Myra was venerated as a wonder-worker and patron of sailors and children, and from 1087 his shrine at Bari drew pilgrims.
The first seasonal manger scene, enacted rather than sculpted, is attributed to Francis of Assisi, who is said to have staged it in a cave near Greccio in 1223.
Christmas hymns may be traced to 4th-century Rome and the earliest English carols to a manuscript of 1426; carols grew in popularity after the Reformation.
The decorated evergreen was first recorded among German Lutherans in the 16th century, and in Britain Queen Charlotte introduced a tree in 1800.
The gift-bringer of Christmas Eve derives from Saint Nicholas and the Dutch Sinterklaas; an 1823 poem with a sleigh and flying reindeer laid the foundation of his modern image.
Dickens's novella of the miser Scrooge and the three spirits was published on 19 December 1843, sold out by Christmas Eve and has never been out of print.
